summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history of sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, TPN dependence via femoral catheter, and recurrent line infections was admitted for fever, chills, and erythema at her left femoral line site with purulent discharge. She was started on IV vancomycin for suspected catheter-related infection. Blood cultures were negative, and a chest X-ray showed no pneumonia. Due to contraindication from a spinal stimulator, an MRV was not performed. The infected left femoral catheter was removed and replaced with a new tunneled line in the right femoral vein. The catheter tip culture later showed no growth. TPN was held during admission and will be resumed at home. Antibiotics were discontinued at discharge. She remained afebrile, with stable labs and controlled symptoms. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor the new line site and resume her prior medication and TPN regimen.
